title: Movement, case order and cleaning between cases in the theatre
audience: Operating-theatre staff and cleaning contractors who clean the theatre between cases. Contractors follow the cleaning steps in this lesson and the theatre own instructions.
learningOutcomes: Explain how closed doors and controlled movement reduce airborne contamination during a case.
Describe how the order of cases on a list can make cleaning more effective.
Carry out the between-case clean for a theatre table and touch surfaces, including clearing away blood and any other fluid.

instruction.heading: Where microbes in a theatre come from
instruction.body: According to the operating-theatre paper, germs that enter an open, clean wound come from the skin of the patient, from the hand of the surgeon, or from airborne microbes that land in the wound or on tools. The bulk of airborne microbes in a theatre originate with the team members, while the patient contributes only a small share. The number of microbes dispersed rises with movement. Managing traffic through the room is therefore part of infection control. Doors should stay shut so the air handling works as designed, and foot traffic should be kept to the lowest level while a procedure runs.

instruction.heading: The order of cases on the list
instruction.body: The same paper requires that the operating table and any items touching the patient are cleaned between one person and the next. It observes that scheduling a case that sheds many microbes at the close of the list can simplify cleaning, although that order is unnecessary when the between-patient clean already does its job. The learner guide principle that work moves from clean to contaminated supports the same approach. Follow the list order that the facility sets.

instruction.heading: What the between-case clean involves
instruction.body: The theatre document calls routine cleaning adequate between cases. The learner guide sets the method for a between-patient wipe. It uses a mild detergent solution, a single-use towel, a sequence from the least soiled surface to the most soiled, disinfection where the facility requires it, and a final drying pass. Routine cleaning counts as adequate only when it includes this wipe. The learner guide governs the method.

instruction.heading: Blood, body fluid and instruments
instruction.body: Wipe blood and any other organic matter from kit, walls and floors promptly. Before instruments travel to central processing in a sealed container, knock off heavy soil in the theatre. Use mechanical washing where practicable. If machine washing is not possible, wash by hand in a basin of warm detergent solution, never beneath a running tap. The learner guide sets a ceiling of thirty-five degrees for preliminary cleaning. Immerse instruments before scrubbing, and never scrub them while any part of them sits above the water.

instruction.heading: Containing fluids and handling specimens
instruction.body: Fluids from the patient are kept inside a liquid-proof drape or a sealed suction set, ideally disposable. This is a clinical measure. Samples and tissue pieces are placed in leak-proof tubs or biohazard bags before they are carried away. Swabs and sponges soaked in blood sit in a basin until the theatre team counts them and seals them in a plastic sack. Cleaners do not count swabs. Specimens are carried only by staff the facility has authorised.

instruction.heading: Surgical steps not used here
instruction.body: Closing and drainage steps and wound dressings in the theatre document are surgical technique and are not used in this lesson.

procedure: Confirm that the patient has left the room and that the team has finished with the table.
Put on the protective items the theatre plan requires (see “Theatre attire, gloves, footwear and jewellery”).
Move used items to the contaminated receiving area, and keep clean items apart from them.
Wipe the table and touch surfaces from least to most soiled, using a mild detergent solution and a single-use towel. Disinfect where the facility plan requires it.
Take away visible blood or fluid straight away. Clean any walls and floors that were splashed, and dry all surfaces.
Discard the towels, take off the gloves, clean your hands, and tick the checklist.

workedExamples.situation: Two cases are booked back to back, and the first has heavy body fluid loss.
workedExamples.reasoning: Follow the list order and the facility plan. Remove the visible fluid at once, wipe the table and contact surfaces in the stated order with the approved method, and do not rely on a quick look to show the surface is clean.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner is asked to wipe the table with a damp cloth, and no detergent is used because the table looks clean.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The method needs a detergent wipe and a disposable towel, and the appearance of the table is not proof that it is clean.

equipmentAndPpe: Neutral detergent and warm water, or the facility product for the surface
Disposable paper towel and fresh cloths for each area
Fluid-resistant gown or apron, gloves and eye protection, as the plan lists
Labelled, sealed waste bags and a lidded box for instruments

commonErrors.error: Opening the theatre door during a case for convenience.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep doors closed and limit movement during procedures.

commonErrors.error: Wiping the table with a dirty cloth.
commonErrors.prevention: Use disposable towels, and a fresh cloth for each area.

commonErrors.error: Leaving blood on the floor until the list finishes.
commonErrors.prevention: Remove visible fluid at once, as the theatre procedure requires.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Specimen transport is limited to staff the facility has authorised under its procedure. This lesson does not authorise anyone to transport specimens or clinical waste.
Stop work if a sharp is found, if a spill goes beyond the facility limit, or if a cut or glove tear occurs.
Completing this lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority to perform regulated work.

qualityStandard: Learner explains how door control and controlled movement reduce risk.
Learner sequences the between-case steps, including the detergent wipe and the disposable towel.
Learner states the cleaning method for instruments and the rule for the water used.
documentationEvidence: Between-case checklist, with each step ticked, the theatre and the time recorded.
Record of any spill cleaned, with the product used and the person told.
summary: Closed doors and limited movement reduce airborne contamination.
The between-case clean is a detergent wipe with a disposable towel, followed by disinfection where the plan requires it.
Visible fluid is cleared straight away, and only authorised staff handle specimens.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why are theatre doors kept closed during a procedure?
options: To keep the room warm for the team and to keep the air still for the team
To support the ventilation system and reduce movement that spreads microbes
To stop the patient from hearing the team and to keep the lights on
To make the case last longer and to keep the surgeon busy with the team

knowledgeChecks.question: Between two cases, what must the clean include for the table and contact surfaces?
options: A quick look and a dry cloth, a fast look at the bench, the rails and the lamp
A detergent wipe with a disposable towel, and disinfection where the facility plan requires it
Only the floor, mopped with the same cloth used on the table, and the table is then left wet
Water alone, poured straight from the tap onto the table and then left to dry in the air

knowledgeChecks.question: How should instruments with gross soiling be handled before transport to the central processing area?
options: Left in the sink until the day is over with the water left in and the lid off
Heavy soil rinsed off in the theatre, then packed in a sealed box for the trip
Packed dry in the surgical pack and sent straight to the store for the day
Washed under running water on the trolley and then left to air-dry there

Conflict and resolution: the theatre document calls routine cleaning adequate between cases; the learner guide specifies the between-patient wipe method, which governs. The theatre preference for warm water is refined by the learner guide 35 degree figure, which is UNCONFIRMED.
Cross-checked against HCG-10 (spill management) and HLT-09 (cleaning sequence); no external source checked. The authorised-staff rule for specimens is general practice, not taken from either source.
